decisions.reason: The accent remains deferred and its rule to derive from the eventually resolved Hero V geometry remains valid; the new Hero V exploration does not change that rule.
The second V must still grow from the resolved Hero V geometry and remain part of the same V system; changing the Hero V design direction does not alter that dependency.
The source applies refined, architectural, elevated, and harmonious qualities to the Hero V without changing the existing identity-wide expression requirements.
The source changes exploration of the Hero V only and does not revise the deferred complete-wordmark rhythm, kerning, or visual hierarchy.
The Hero V geometry change does not alter the deferred champagne-metal treatment, its desired qualities, or the requirement to resolve geometry before applying material.
The source concerns fresh concepts for the Hero V and does not change the deferred construction or visual language of the remaining wordmark letterforms.
Although the source broadens exploration beyond isolated right-arm geometry, it preserves the existing structural, deliberate, and non-decorative terminal principles rather than replacing them.
Exploring a new complete Hero V form does not change the wordmark-led identity, the absence of a separate icon or monogram, or the opening V's standalone brand role.
